title: The Peacock and the Sun (U Klew Bad Ka Sngi)
cultural_context: The primordial Khasi myth of the Peacock's unrequited love for Ka Sngi (the Sun), set to lyrical verse in 'Ki Jingrwai Khasi'.
lyrics_khasi:
U klew u peit sha suiñ,
Sha khet ka sngi ba phyrnai,
U pynpaw la ki sner
Ba itynnad ban rwai;
U kwah ban poi sha bneng
Sha tmier ka khet ka jingshai,
Ban shong lang bad ka sngi
Ha dohnud ba kynjai.

Hynrei ka sngi ka jngai,
Sha lyndet ki lum bakhraw,
U klew u shad pynran
Ha madan lum ba paw;
Ki khmat ha ki sner jong u
Ki thaba kynmaw sngi,
Ha man ka por ba mih
Ka kynjat jingshai thymmai.
lyrics_english:
The peacock gazes heavenward,
Toward the radiant throne of the Sun,
Unfolding his glittering plumes
In splendour fit for song;
Yearning to reach the skies
To the rim of the solar throne,
To dwell alongside the Sun
In undisturbed serenity.

Yet the Sun remains far off,
Beyond the great mountain crests,
The peacock dances on the ridge
Visible against high hills;
The eye-gems upon his plumes
Shine in remembrance of the Sun,
Each time the dawn casts forth
Her rays of living light.
